content: Bronchiectasis is increasingly being recognized as a co-morbidity in various respiratory illnesses. Anti-inflammatory drugs have the potential to mitigate the inflammatory cascade, which may help alleviate symptoms and slow the progression of long-term pulmonary decline. The objective of this study was to evaluate the role of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) in controlling symptoms and influencing the natural course of bronchiectasis in both children and adults. To achieve this, a comprehensive search was conducted by the Cochrane Airways Group across multiple databases, including the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL), the Cochrane Airways Group Specialised Register, MEDLINE, and EMBASE, up until December 2008. The inclusion criteria were limited to randomized controlled trials (RCTs). Participants were required to have radiological or clinical evidence of bronchiectasis, while individuals with cystic fibrosis were excluded from the analysis. Two independent reviewers assessed the titles, abstracts, and citations to determine their relevance for a full review. However, no eligible randomized controlled trials were identified, and as a result, no data were available for analysis. The main finding of this review is that no randomized or controlled trials have been conducted to evaluate the effects of oral NSAIDs in patients with bronchiectasis. Given the evidence of some benefit from inhaled NSAIDs in bronchiectasis, there is a clear need for randomized controlled trials to investigate the potential therapeutic effects of oral NSAIDs in this patient population.
